steps.x: The analyst signs in through Easy Auth. Only members of the assigned group get a session; the token requested at sign-in is for the API's scope.

steps.t: Call the API as the analyst
steps.x: The frontend's proxy forwards /api with the analyst's bearer token. The API checks issuer, audience and scope, then which clients this user may see. No token: 401.
Screens read tcc_gold (figures) and tcc_ops (claims and engagements) from the Warehouse as the API's managed identity. No calculation runs on a page load.

scenarios.title: A calculation run for one client

steps.x: The API reads that client's Delta tables from the Lakehouse over OneLake. Payroll stays in memory; nothing copies it into the Warehouse.
The engine applies the rule pack frozen for each tax year and records every step with its inputs, formula, citation and a SHA-256 over the trail.
Gold rows and the run manifest are written together; the prior run's rows are marked not current, never overwritten. A write-write conflict is retried.
The API answers the question with deterministic code before any model is involved.
An aggregate brief (no payroll rows, names or per-person figures) goes to a Foundry agent, which writes the explanation. If Foundry is unreachable, every screen still works.
If the customer requires it, agent traffic routes through their AI gateway. It must carry the Foundry Agents protocol.

scenarios.title: A claim package, generated and downloaded

steps.x: The API renders the package and writes it to outputs/{client_id}/{run_id}/ through the blob private endpoint, then records it in tcc_ops.artifact with its SHA-256.
The analyst asks for the file through the app. The API checks the user may see that client and that the artifact row exists.
The API streams the blob and writes tcc_ops.artifact_access (served, denied or missing). The storage account itself is unreachable from outside: no public access, no shared key, no SAS.
Terraform creates both managed identities and assigns their Azure roles: Blob Data Contributor, Foundry User, Monitoring Metrics Publisher.

The workspace role for the API identity can be assigned by Terraform's Fabric provider, or by the customer if they own Fabric access. Schema-level read/write on tcc_gold and tcc_ops is a T-SQL grant run after deploy.
The customer creates the app registrations and assigns the analyst group. Terraform only takes their client IDs.
Every pull request runs both suites with the parity gate required: 10,236 evaluated, 539 Min-Max, 656 Pay Period.
The workflow exchanges its GitHub token for an Entra token. No secret is stored anywhere.
terraform apply, then zip deploy of the API and the built frontend. Re-running is a no-op.
